title: Parity-Based Binary String Flipping Strategy
approach_explanation:
The problem asks us to make all bits in a binary string equal to 0 by choosing indices such that choosing index $i$ flips all other elements except $i$. Notice that if we pick a set of indices $S$, an element $j$ will be flipped $|S| - 1$ times if $j

If we perform a subset of operations on all 1s, the parity of flips on each bit can be analyzed. Specifically, if we perform operations at all indices containing '1', every '1' position is left unflipped an extra time relative to the total number of operations, or similar parity invariants emerge. Based on the count of '0's and '1's and their parities, we can partition cases: (1) If there are no '1's, 0 operations suffice. (2) If there is exactly 1 '0', we can pick that '0'. (3) If the total count of '1's is even, choosing all '1' indices works. (4) If the total count of '0's is odd, choosing all '0' indices works. Otherwise, it's impossible (-1).

code_breakdown.explanation: Read the test cases loop, reading $n$ and the string $s$. Count the total number of '0's and '1's.
If there are 0 ones, output 0. If there is exactly 1 zero, output 1 and the 1-based index of that zero.

Check if the number of ones is even. If so, output the count and print all 1-indexed positions where $s[i] == '1'$. Otherwise, check if the number of zeros is odd. If so, output the count and print all 1-indexed positions where $s[i] == '0'$. If neither holds, output -1.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: We iterate through the string of length $N$ a constant number of times per test case to count characters and print indices. Sum of $N$ over all test cases is $\le 2 \cdot 10^5$, giving an optimal linear runtime.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: The string $s$ of length $N$ is stored in memory for each test case.

strengths: Linear time complexity per test case
Clear branching logic based on mathematical insights
